page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.large is a compute-optimized virtual machine provisioned via the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, featuring 1 physical core and 2 hardware threads (2 vCPUs). It is configured with 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), 32 MB of L3 cache, and a dedicated CPU allocation. The underlying processor includes vector instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, along with cryptographic features including AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The server contains no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on remote disk storage and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate sharp divergence between single-threaded and aggregate multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core performance is robust, with stress-ng placing in the top 10% and Geekbench single-core reaching the top 25% (1997.0). However, overall multi-core throughput is constrained by the small total core count of 2 vCPUs, resulting in lower-tier placement across multi-threaded metrics such as PassMark CPU (3870.88), Geekbench multi-core (2481.0), and Clang compilation (2849.0). Memory bandwidth behaves moderately under large uncached blocks at 47.32 GB/sec read and 27.49 GB/sec write, but database operations and static web serving rank in lower percentiles.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, ecs.c8ae.large provides dedicated access to modern Zen-based CPU instructions without the multi-tenant resource contention seen in shared-core instances. The compact 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio keeps resource density focused on lightweight processing tasks. Primary operational tradeoffs stem from the absence of local NVMe storage, a 4 GB RAM footprint, and multi-thread limits driven by the dual-vCPU ceiling. Workload suitability centers on entry-level compute tasks, single-threaded processing pipelines, lightweight microservices, and modest utility services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz. It delivers 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core, 4.0 GB of RAM, and 32 MB of L3 cache, operating over a 3 Gbps baseline network. Bundled local storage and hardware GPU acceleration are not included. The processor supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and VAES. Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-core execution, ranking in the upper quartile for Geekbench and the top 10% for stress-ng single-core tasks. Multi-core performance and total throughput are modest, bounded by the dual-thread ceiling. With its 1:2 compute-focused memory ratio, ecs.c8ae.large is best suited for lightweight compute tasks, microservices, and single-threaded batch processing.
